calls.head: The Kraken better keep their heads up
calls.body: The Sharks hit a lot, but the Kraken mostly don’t. San Jose is one of the league’s best for physicality, and Seattle is one of the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. Expect most of the big hits to come from the Sharks.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Orlov has three assists as the Sharks get past the Kraken
paras: The first period was a wild one. Ryker Evans struck first for the Kraken on the power play early in the period. Michael Misa and Nolan Allan scored just over four minutes apart later in the period to turn a 1-0 deficit into a 2-1 lead. San Jose had a goal taken off for goalie interference late in the first, but it didn’t cost them in the end. Macklin Celebrini pushed the lead to 3-1 on the power play later in the period. Ivar Stenberg made it 4-1 on the power play early in the second, and that insurance goal turned out to be the winner. Matty Beniers cut San Jose’s lead to 4-2 a little over three minutes later, and Ryan Winterton pulled the Kraken within one late in the period. Dmitry Orlov finished with three assists.

The chances were close to even, so this one could have gone either way. Alex Nedeljkovic made 27 saves for the Sharks, and Philipp Grubauer stopped 24 of 28 at the other end. By our Swing measure, Alexander Wennberg had the best night of anyone, even without a point. The Sharks improved to 11-12-2 and climbed to third in the Pacific, while the Kraken dropped to 10-9-1, slipping to sixth in the Pacific.

items.text: Macklin Celebrini extended his point streak against Seattle to eight games.
Matty Beniers has scored in three straight games.
The Kraken have gone winless in five straight on the road.
Brett Leason made his Sharks debut, after two seasons with the Capitals.
